banner.title: loki
banner.tagline: Keeps every container log for 14 days on one Ceph volume and answers the LogQL queries Grafana sends it.

art.about: how a log line travels from a pod into Loki and back out to a query
art.title: How Loki stores and serves logs

explainer.title: From a log line to a LogQL answer

steps.title: Receive
steps.text: Promtail pushes batches to loki-headless on port 3100. The NetworkPolicy admits only monitoring, rook-ceph and DNS replies.
steps.scene: log lines arriving through a funnel

steps.title: Chunk
steps.text: The ingester holds streams in memory and a WAL under /var/loki/wal, then cuts chunks of snappy-compressed blocks, 256 KiB each.
steps.scene: stacked log chunks forming a small tower

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Chunks and the TSDB index, schema v13, live on a 50 GiB ceph-block volume. With no object store, that volume is the whole data set.
steps.scene: a storage cylinder beside an index card

steps.title: Expire
steps.text: The compactor deletes streams past 14 days. Ingest is capped at 10 MB/s with a 20 MB burst.
steps.scene: an hourglass over a stack of expired log pages

steps.title: Query
steps.text: Grafana's Loki datasource sends LogQL to port 3100. Loki's own request metrics feed three alerts.
steps.scene: a magnifying glass over log lines
